newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia mobster jailed for 1989 political slaying.
newsitem.headline: Colombia mobster jailed for 1989 political slaying.

text.p: A former henchman of Colombia's Medellin drug mob was sentenced to 40 years jail for the 1989 murder of leading presidential candidate Luis Carlos Galan, judicial sources said on Friday.
John Jairo Velasquez, alias Popeye, is the first person to be convicted of the killing, which was carried out as Galan addressed a political rally in Soacha just outside the capital Bogota.
The attack, which shook the nation, is believed to have been ordered by the late Medellin cartel boss Pablo Escobar and his head of "military" operations Gonzalo Rodriguez Gacha.

"This is the first conviction in the eight years since Galan was assassinated," a spokesman at the Chief Prosecutor's department said. "The form in which the killing was carried out and the criminal structure of the organisation makes it very difficult to investigate," he added.

Velasquez's 40-year term was immediately cut to 26 years after he confessed to his part in setting up and planning the killing. He is currently in Bogota's maximum security La Modelo jail serving a 30-year term for terrorism, drug trafficking and organising paramilitary groups.
At least six other people are under investigation for the Galan killing, judicial sources said.
Galan, a 46-year-old former senator, was running for the 1990 presidential elections representing his New Liberalism movement, an influential dissident faction of the mainstream Liberal Party.
One of the central planks of his election platform was his drive against Colombia's all-powerful cocaine cartels and their corrupt hold on politics.
On the night he was shot, Galan was wearing a bullet-proof vest but it rode up as he raised his arms to salute the crowd, allowing bullets to pass underneath.

Two other presidential candidates, Carlos Pizarro of the demobilized M-19 guerrilla movement, and Bernardo Jaramillo of the leftist Patriotic Union (UP) party, were also killed in the lead-up to the 1990 ballot.
